quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that paraphrase the story accurately, and put them in order.
quests.story: The kitchen renovation at the Moreau family's house was meant to take two weeks, but the plumber found rotten pipes behind the old sink. The builders replaced the pipes under the floor, which added ten days. The family cooked on a camping stove until the new hob was fitted.
options: Replacing the pipes under the floor added ten days to the work.
The plumber discovered rotten pipes behind the old sink, which put the two-week schedule at risk.
Replacing the pipes under the floor added a whole month to the building work.
Until the new hob went in, the family cooked on a camping stove.
quests.hint: A paraphrase can change the words but not the numbers. Compare every amount with the story.
quests.explanation: The story says the pipe replacement added ten days, and "a month" stretches that. An accurate paraphrase may reword the sentence but keeps the length of the delay.
storyKeyEvents: The plumber discovered rotten pipes behind the old sink, which put the two-week schedule at risk.
Replacing the pipes under the floor added ten days to the work.
Until the new hob went in, the family cooked on a camping stove.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Dr. Karlsson's guest lecture was moved from Tuesday to Thursday because it clashed with a faculty meeting. The department emailed the students and updated the lecture theatre booking. About eighty students came on Thursday, and Dr. Karlsson said she might return next year.
options: Around eighty students attended on Thursday.
The department told the students by email and changed the theatre booking.
Dr. Karlsson promised the department that she would return next year.
A clash with a faculty meeting caused Dr. Karlsson's lecture to be moved to Thursday.
quests.hint: Words like "might" and "promised" carry different levels of certainty.
quests.explanation: She said she might return, which is a possibility, while "promised" turns it into a commitment. A paraphrase must keep how certain the original is.
storyKeyEvents: A clash with a faculty meeting caused Dr. Karlsson's lecture to be moved to Thursday.
The department told the students by email and changed the theatre booking.
Around eighty students attended on Thursday.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The council approved the mural on the library wall after the artist showed sketches to a residents' meeting. Painting took three weekends, and a local paint shop donated the materials. Residents said the wall no longer attracted graffiti.
options: The council approved the mural because a local shop had offered to donate the paint.
The painting was done over three weekends with materials given by a local shop.
Once the artist presented sketches at a residents' meeting, the council approved the mural.
Residents reported that graffiti no longer appeared on the wall.
quests.hint: Check the reason given for each decision. Does the paraphrase keep it?
quests.explanation: The story links the approval to the sketches shown at the meeting, not to the paint donation. Changing the reason changes the meaning even if every fact in the sentence appears elsewhere.
storyKeyEvents: Once the artist presented sketches at a residents' meeting, the council approved the mural.
The painting was done over three weekends with materials given by a local shop.
Residents reported that graffiti no longer appeared on the wall.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Sven house-sat his neighbour's cat for a fortnight. He fed it twice a day and cleaned the litter tray, and when the cat stopped eating on the fifth day he phoned the vet. The vet said the cat only disliked the new food, so Sven went back to the old brand.
options: When the cat refused food on day five, Sven called the vet.
The vet thought the cat simply disliked the new food, so Sven returned to the old brand.
For two weeks Sven cared for his neighbour's cat, feeding it twice daily.
Sven phoned the vet every day after the cat stopped eating on day five.
quests.hint: Watch for frequency words like "every day" that stretch a single event.
quests.explanation: Sven phoned the vet once, on the fifth day. Repeating it daily turns one call into a routine the story never mentions.
storyKeyEvents: For two weeks Sven cared for his neighbour's cat, feeding it twice daily.
When the cat refused food on day five, Sven called the vet.
The vet thought the cat simply disliked the new food, so Sven returned to the old brand.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Snowfall cut off the mountain cabin on Friday night. On Saturday morning the guests dug a path to the shed, and by noon they had found the generator's fuel can. The road crew reached the cabin on Sunday afternoon.
options: Heavy snow isolated the cabin on Friday night.
By Saturday noon the guests had cleared a path to the shed and located the generator's fuel.
The road crew reached the cabin on Saturday afternoon, before the guests found the fuel.
The road crew arrived on Sunday afternoon.
quests.hint: Check whether the order of events survives the rewording.
quests.explanation: The crew came on Sunday, after the guests had found the fuel on Saturday. Moving it earlier reverses the sequence.
storyKeyEvents: Heavy snow isolated the cabin on Friday night.
By Saturday noon the guests had cleared a path to the shed and located the generator's fuel.
The road crew arrived on Sunday afternoon.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Hannah applied for a resident parking permit. The council asked her to send a utility bill as proof of address, and Hannah's landlord emailed a copy of the bill the next day. The permit arrived by post ten days later.
options: Hannah made an application for a resident parking permit.
The permit came in the post ten days afterwards.
The council wanted proof of her address, and her landlord emailed a copy of a utility bill.
Hannah's landlord applied for the parking permit on her behalf.
quests.hint: A rewording can quietly change who does what.
quests.explanation: Hannah applied herself; her landlord only supplied a copy of the bill. Giving the landlord the application changes the actor.
storyKeyEvents: Hannah made an application for a resident parking permit.
The council wanted proof of her address, and her landlord emailed a copy of a utility bill.
The permit came in the post ten days afterwards.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The bus company introduced a new travel card that replaced paper tickets. Commuters were reluctant at first, but queues at the ticket office shortened within a month, and most people switched. The company then removed the ticket machines from three stops.
options: Commuters welcomed the new card enthusiastically from the very start.
Once most people had switched, the company took ticket machines out of three stops.
Commuters were hesitant at first, yet ticket-office queues shrank within a month.
A new travel card took the place of paper tickets on the buses.
quests.hint: Notice how the passenger's attitude is described, not just what they did.
quests.explanation: The story says commuters were reluctant at first, which "welcomed from the start" reverses. Attitude words are part of the meaning.
storyKeyEvents: A new travel card took the place of paper tickets on the buses.
Commuters were hesitant at first, yet ticket-office queues shrank within a month.
Once most people had switched, the company took ticket machines out of three stops.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: An amateur film festival ran short of seats when an unexpected crowd arrived on opening night. Volunteers fetched extra chairs from the church hall, and the screening started fifteen minutes late. Most of the audience stayed for the whole programme.
options: Most of the audience remained until the end of the programme.
More people than expected came on opening night, leaving too few seats.
The screening was delayed by more than an hour while the chairs were fetched.
Volunteers brought extra chairs from the church hall, so the screening began a quarter of an hour late.
quests.hint: A small delay and a long delay are different facts. Which does the story give?
quests.explanation: The screening began fifteen minutes late, and "more than an hour" exaggerates it. A paraphrase should match the size of a delay.
storyKeyEvents: More people than expected came on opening night, leaving too few seats.
Volunteers brought extra chairs from the church hall, so the screening began a quarter of an hour late.
Most of the audience remained until the end of the programme.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Nadeem asked the shop for a refund on a coat with a broken zip. The manager said the shop could not refund items after thirty days, but he offered a repair instead. Nadeem accepted, and the coat was returned to him within a week.
options: The manager refused the refund and also refused to repair the coat.
Nadeem requested a refund for a coat whose zip had broken.
Nadeem agreed, and he had the coat back within a week.
The manager could not refund the coat after thirty days, but offered to repair it.
quests.hint: Look at the word "but". What contrast does it set up?
quests.explanation: The manager refused the refund but did offer a repair, so "also refused to repair" removes the offer. The contrast in the original is what makes the story work.
storyKeyEvents: Nadeem requested a refund for a coat whose zip had broken.
The manager could not refund the coat after thirty days, but offered to repair it.
Nadeem agreed, and he had the coat back within a week.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The carpool app kept assigning Dilan and his colleague Amira to different cars. Dilan reported the fault to the app's support team, who found that the two of them had listed different home addresses. Once Dilan corrected his address, they were matched to the same car.
options: Support discovered that the two had entered different home addresses.
After Dilan fixed his address, the app put them in the same car.
The carpool app kept placing Dilan and Amira in separate cars.
Support apologised and gave both of them a month of free rides.
quests.hint: A paraphrase should add nothing new. Does each option come from the text?
quests.explanation: The apology and free rides never appear in the story. An accurate paraphrase repeats what the text says and doesn't add extras.
storyKeyEvents: The carpool app kept placing Dilan and Amira in separate cars.
Support discovered that the two had entered different home addresses.
After Dilan fixed his address, the app put them in the same car.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: A volunteer tutoring programme paired Kofi with a ten-year-old who struggled with reading. Kofi brought short comics to the sessions, and after six weeks the boy was reading a page aloud without help. The coordinator said the boy would probably move up a reading group in the spring.
options: The coordinator confirmed that the boy would move up a reading group in the spring.
Kofi was matched with a ten-year-old who found reading difficult.
Kofi brought short comics to their sessions.
Six weeks later the boy could read a page aloud unaided.
quests.hint: "Probably" and "confirmed" don't mean the same thing.
quests.explanation: The coordinator only said the move was probable. Saying it was confirmed makes an expectation into a fact.
storyKeyEvents: Kofi was matched with a ten-year-old who found reading difficult.
Kofi brought short comics to their sessions.
Six weeks later the boy could read a page aloud unaided.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The pool at the community centre was losing water faster than expected. The caretaker measured a drop of three centimetres overnight and called a specialist, who found a crack near the drain. The pool was closed for two weeks while the crack was sealed.
options: A specialist called by the caretaker found a crack near the drain.
The caretaker measured a drop of thirty centimetres overnight.
The pool was losing water faster than it should have.
The pool stayed shut for a fortnight while the crack was sealed.
quests.hint: Measurements are easy to distort. Compare them carefully.
quests.explanation: The drop was three centimetres, and thirty would be ten times greater. The rest of the statement is accurate, which makes the change easy to miss.
storyKeyEvents: The pool was losing water faster than it should have.
A specialist called by the caretaker found a crack near the drain.
The pool stayed shut for a fortnight while the crack was sealed.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: At the society fair the chess club had the smallest stand. Members played quick games with passers-by, which drew crowds. By the end of the day sixty-three students had signed up, more than for any other society.
options: The chess club had the most sign-ups because its stand was the largest.
By playing quick games with passers-by, members attracted crowds.
By closing time sixty-three students had signed up, more than any other society.
The chess club's stand was the smallest at the fair.
quests.hint: One detail here is turned into its opposite. Find the word that flips.
quests.explanation: The stand was the smallest, and the sign-ups came from the games rather than from size. The statement reverses both the fact and the reason.
storyKeyEvents: The chess club's stand was the smallest at the fair.
By playing quick games with passers-by, members attracted crowds.
By closing time sixty-three students had signed up, more than any other society.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Miriam's first week as a manager began with a two-day induction. On Wednesday she met each member of her team one by one, and on Thursday she took over the weekly planning meeting. On Friday the director told her the team's targets would be reviewed in a month.
options: Miriam started her time as manager with two days of induction.
On Wednesday she held one-to-one meetings with each team member.
Miriam ran the weekly planning meeting before she had her induction.
On Thursday she took charge of the weekly planning meeting.
quests.hint: Look at where the induction sits in the week, and where the planning meeting sits.
quests.explanation: The induction came first, at the beginning of the week, and the planning meeting on Thursday. Putting the meeting before it reverses the sequence.
storyKeyEvents: Miriam started her time as manager with two days of induction.
On Wednesday she held one-to-one meetings with each team member.
On Thursday she took charge of the weekly planning meeting.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: A timetable clash left Idris with two lectures at the same hour. He emailed the course office, and the office moved one lecture to the following morning. Idris's classmate Berit told him about the change before the notice went up.
options: After his email, the course office rescheduled one lecture for the next morning.
His classmate Berit told him of the change before it was officially posted.
Berit emailed the course office, and the office then moved one lecture.
Idris found he had two lectures scheduled for the same hour.
quests.hint: A statement can contain the right events attached to the wrong person.
quests.explanation: Idris wrote to the office, and Berit only passed on the news. Swapping them changes who set things in motion.
storyKeyEvents: Idris found he had two lectures scheduled for the same hour.
After his email, the course office rescheduled one lecture for the next morning.
His classmate Berit told him of the change before it was officially posted.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The marketing team launched a campaign for a new water bottle on Monday. Posts on social media reached about thirty thousand people in the first week, and two of the largest retailers asked for samples. By the end of the month the first batch of bottles had sold out.
options: The team began the water-bottle campaign on Monday.
In the first week the posts reached around thirty thousand people, and two of the biggest retailers requested samples.
The first batch had sold out by the end of the month.
Every major retailer asked for samples in the first week.
quests.hint: Look for words such as "every" that widen a number.
quests.explanation: Only two of the largest retailers asked for samples, so "every major retailer" widens the group. The size of the group is part of the fact.
storyKeyEvents: The team began the water-bottle campaign on Monday.
In the first week the posts reached around thirty thousand people, and two of the biggest retailers requested samples.
The first batch had sold out by the end of the month.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The coffee roaster's usual bean supplier delayed a shipment by four days. The owner bought a small emergency lot from another importer and adjusted the recipe slightly so the taste stayed close to the original. Regular customers noticed no difference.
options: Regular customers could not tell the difference.
The owner bought a small emergency lot elsewhere and tweaked the recipe a little to keep the taste.
The owner completely changed the recipe to suit the new beans.
The regular bean supplier's shipment was four days late.
quests.hint: "Slightly" and "completely" describe very different amounts of change.
quests.explanation: The recipe was adjusted slightly to keep the taste close to the original. A complete change would contradict that aim.
storyKeyEvents: The regular bean supplier's shipment was four days late.
The owner bought a small emergency lot elsewhere and tweaked the recipe a little to keep the taste.
Regular customers could not tell the difference.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: A bookshop planned a reading evening with a local novelist. The owner, Marta, asked the novelist to read for twenty minutes only, because the shop's chairs were uncomfortable, and she agreed with a laugh. The evening ran over anyway, since the audience asked so many questions.
options: The bookshop arranged a reading evening with a local novelist.
The evening overran because the audience had so many questions.
Marta asked the novelist to limit her reading to twenty minutes, and the novelist agreed cheerfully.
The novelist reluctantly accepted the twenty-minute time limit, frowning.
quests.hint: Notice how the novelist reacts. Which word describes it?
quests.explanation: She agreed with a laugh, which suggests good humour rather than reluctance. Attitude is part of what a paraphrase must keep.
storyKeyEvents: The bookshop arranged a reading evening with a local novelist.
Marta asked the novelist to limit her reading to twenty minutes, and the novelist agreed cheerfully.
The evening overran because the audience had so many questions.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Ella's gym locker was jammed on Monday. The desk staff tried a master key without success, but the maintenance worker opened it with a small tool in two minutes. Ella got her bag back and switched to a different locker.
options: The desk staff opened the locker with a master key, and maintenance later repaired it.
Ella retrieved her bag and moved to another locker.
Ella's locker jammed on Monday.
The master key did not work, but a maintenance worker opened the locker in two minutes.
quests.hint: Ask who succeeded and who failed.
quests.explanation: The master key failed, and maintenance was the one who opened the locker. The statement swaps success and failure.
storyKeyEvents: Ella's locker jammed on Monday.
The master key did not work, but a maintenance worker opened the locker in two minutes.
Ella retrieved her bag and moved to another locker.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: A tram strike left thousands of commuters stranded on Tuesday. Employers allowed staff to work from home, and the city added extra buses on the busiest routes. The strike ended on Thursday after a late-night agreement.
options: A late-night agreement ended the strike on Thursday.
The city refunded tram fares for the whole week to all commuters.
Employers let staff work from home, and the city put extra buses on its busiest routes.
Thousands of commuters were stuck on Tuesday because of a tram strike.
quests.hint: Would you find this sentence in the story if you searched for it?
quests.explanation: Nothing in the story mentions refunds. An accurate paraphrase can't introduce new events.
storyKeyEvents: Thousands of commuters were stuck on Tuesday because of a tram strike.
Employers let staff work from home, and the city put extra buses on its busiest routes.
A late-night agreement ended the strike on Thursday.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: A street artist asked a café owner for permission to paint the side wall. The owner said she would think about it and wanted to see a sketch first. The artist brought a sketch the next morning, and the owner agreed.
options: The next morning the artist showed a sketch, and the owner agreed.
A street artist requested permission to paint the café's side wall.
The owner said she'd think it over and asked to see a sketch first.
The owner told the artist she would definitely allow the painting on the wall.
quests.hint: How certain is the owner's first answer?
quests.explanation: She said she would think about it, which leaves the decision open. "Definitely allow" turns her hesitation into a promise.
storyKeyEvents: A street artist requested permission to paint the café's side wall.
The owner said she'd think it over and asked to see a sketch first.
The next morning the artist showed a sketch, and the owner agreed.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Farida's flat had no hot water for three days. The landlord blamed the boiler, but the engineer found that a tenant upstairs had closed a valve by mistake. He reopened the valve, and the hot water returned.
options: Farida went without hot water for three days.
The engineer found that the boiler was broken, as the landlord suspected.
The engineer found that an upstairs tenant had shut a valve by mistake, not that the boiler had failed.
Once he reopened the valve, hot water came back.
quests.hint: Compare what the landlord thought with what the engineer discovered.
quests.explanation: The engineer's finding contradicted the landlord: the valve, not the boiler, was the cause. The statement confirms the wrong explanation.
storyKeyEvents: Farida went without hot water for three days.
The engineer found that an upstairs tenant had shut a valve by mistake, not that the boiler had failed.
Once he reopened the valve, hot water came back.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The school's recycling scheme collected paper from every classroom on Fridays. In its first term it saved about four hundred kilograms of paper, and the caretaker used the money from selling it to buy new bins. The head teacher then asked the canteen to join the scheme.
options: In the first term about four hundred kilograms of paper was saved, and the caretaker spent the sale money on new bins.
The scheme collected all kinds of waste from every classroom.
The head teacher then invited the canteen to take part.
Every Friday, paper was collected from all the classrooms.
quests.hint: Notice what exactly was being collected.
quests.explanation: The scheme collected paper only, so "all kinds of waste" widens what it covered. The scope of the material is part of the fact.
storyKeyEvents: Every Friday, paper was collected from all the classrooms.
In the first term about four hundred kilograms of paper was saved, and the caretaker spent the sale money on new bins.
The head teacher then invited the canteen to take part.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Before boarding the river boat, Jonas showed his ticket to the attendant, who scanned it and pointed him to the upper deck. During the crossing he bought a sandwich at the kiosk. The boat reached the far bank forty minutes late because of strong currents.
options: On the crossing he bought a sandwich from the kiosk.
Jonas had his ticket scanned and was sent to the upper deck.
Strong currents made the boat arrive forty minutes late.
Jonas bought his sandwich at the kiosk before showing his ticket.
quests.hint: Check what came before boarding and what came during the crossing.
quests.explanation: The sandwich was bought during the crossing, after the ticket check at boarding. The statement puts the events the wrong way round.
storyKeyEvents: Jonas had his ticket scanned and was sent to the upper deck.
On the crossing he bought a sandwich from the kiosk.
Strong currents made the boat arrive forty minutes late.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Two neighbours, Lotte and Hugo, disagreed about the hedge between their gardens. Lotte proposed cutting it to one metre, and Hugo suggested sharing the cost of a gardener. They agreed to both ideas and split the bill.
options: The neighbours Lotte and Hugo argued over the hedge between their gardens.
They accepted both suggestions and shared the bill.
Hugo proposed cutting the hedge to one metre, and Lotte suggested sharing the cost.
Lotte wanted to trim the hedge to one metre, and Hugo proposed splitting the cost of a gardener.
quests.hint: The ideas are right but may be given to the wrong people.
quests.explanation: Lotte suggested the height and Hugo the shared cost. The statement swaps their proposals.
storyKeyEvents: The neighbours Lotte and Hugo argued over the hedge between their gardens.
Lotte wanted to trim the hedge to one metre, and Hugo proposed splitting the cost of a gardener.
They accepted both suggestions and shared the bill.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Aditya's laptop battery lasted only about three hours. After the manufacturer released a software update, he installed it, and the battery lasted about five hours.
options: The manufacturer released a software update, which Aditya installed.
Aditya's laptop battery only ran for around three hours.
The battery then lasted more than a full day on a single charge.
Afterwards the battery lasted roughly five hours.
quests.hint: Compare how much the battery improved with what the story says.
quests.explanation: The improvement was from about three to about five hours. "More than a full day" magnifies it far beyond what is stated.
storyKeyEvents: Aditya's laptop battery only ran for around three hours.
The manufacturer released a software update, which Aditya installed.
Afterwards the battery lasted roughly five hours.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The council promised to fix the pothole on Mill Road within a week, but the repair team was diverted to a burst water main. The pothole was finally filled three weeks later, after residents complained again.
options: The hole was filled three weeks later once residents complained again.
The repair team was sent to a burst water main instead.
The council promised to repair the Mill Road pothole within a week.
The council fixed the pothole within a week, even though residents complained.
quests.hint: The word "but" signals a promise that didn't work out.
quests.explanation: The promise was not kept because the team was diverted, and the repair came three weeks later. The statement turns the failed promise into a success.
storyKeyEvents: The council promised to repair the Mill Road pothole within a week.
The repair team was sent to a burst water main instead.
The hole was filled three weeks later once residents complained again.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Yuto entered a photo contest with three pictures. Two were rejected for being too dark, but the third, a street scene at dusk, reached the final round. It finished fourth out of twelve finalists.
options: All three of Yuto's pictures reached the final round.
Two were turned down as too dark.
Yuto submitted three pictures to a photo contest.
The third, a dusk street scene, reached the final and came fourth out of twelve.
quests.hint: Count how many pictures made it through.
quests.explanation: Only one of the three pictures reached the final. Saying all three did contradicts the two rejections.
storyKeyEvents: Yuto submitted three pictures to a photo contest.
Two were turned down as too dark.
The third, a dusk street scene, reached the final and came fourth out of twelve.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: Refilwe was asked to lead the volunteer team at short notice. She accepted after some hesitation and drew up a checklist that evening. By the weekend the team was working smoothly.
options: By the weekend the team was running smoothly.
Refilwe accepted at once and without any doubts.
Refilwe was asked at short notice to lead the volunteers.
After some hesitation she accepted and made a checklist that evening.
quests.hint: Look for how she responded before saying yes.
quests.explanation: She hesitated before accepting, so "at once and without doubts" reverses her reaction. The tone of an acceptance is part of the meaning.
storyKeyEvents: Refilwe was asked at short notice to lead the volunteers.
After some hesitation she accepted and made a checklist that evening.
By the weekend the team was running smoothly.

quests.instruction: Choose the three accurate paraphrases and put them in order.
quests.story: The landlord agreed to repaint the hallway after tenants complained about peeling paint. A painter came on Tuesday and finished in two days. The tenants thanked the landlord in a group message.
options: The landlord agreed to repaint the hallway once tenants complained about peeling paint.
The landlord lowered the rent for a month as an apology to tenants.
The tenants thanked the landlord in a group message.
A painter came on Tuesday and completed the job in two days.
quests.hint: Ask whether each option could be traced to a sentence in the story.
quests.explanation: There is no mention of rent in the story. The painting, the completion, and the thanks are all that is reported.
storyKeyEvents: The landlord agreed to repaint the hallway once tenants complained about peeling paint.
A painter came on Tuesday and completed the job in two days.
The tenants thanked the landlord in a group message.
